themes.name: Critical Thinking Enhancement through GenAI Tools
themes.definition: Integration of generative AI tools to develop critical analysis, argumentation, and reflective evaluation skills across disciplines. Involves comparing information sources, deconstructing problems, and evaluating AI outputs for accuracy.
evidence: [Liu2024c] 'AI-supported SSI model led to significant increases in critical thinking dispositions (p < 0.01) and skills (p < 0.01)'
[Vesali2025] 'enhancing students' critical thinking skills through the students’ feedback and fostering a deeper understanding of AI's role in project scheduling'
[Calderón-Oliver2025] 'facilitating the development of critical thinking by contrasting and evaluating information from various sources'

themes.name: AI-Enhanced Collaborative Learning Models
themes.definition: Use of AI to facilitate group work, peer assessment, and knowledge co-construction. Includes AI-mediated scaffolding for structured collaboration and real-time feedback during team-based tasks.
evidence: [Becerra2025] 'combining AI-driven feedback with dynamic visualization tools to create a holistic assessment process'
[MoslemiNezhadArani2025] 'dynamic scaffold that supports learners’ progression through ill-structured, real-world problem scenarios'
[Agnaou2025] 'investigates whether AI-assisted group work enhances or hinders creativity, critical thinking, and collective intelligence'

themes.name: Pedagogical Integration of AI in Disciplinary Contexts
themes.definition: Application of AI tools within specific academic fields (e.g., STEM, arts, vocational education) to support domain-specific skills through context-sensitive AI integration strategies.
evidence: [Ruiz2025] 'study explores the use of AI as a pedagogical tool to analyze the work of Spanish photographers Alberto Garcia-Alix and Cristina Garcia Rodero'
[Nezhyva2025] 'AI tools were introduced into the teacher preparation curriculum for creating literary-artistic content'
[Lee2025c] 'integrating cultural diversity and AI in a fashion design course to develop product design skills for global markets'

themes.name: AI-Induced Challenges to Cognitive Development
themes.definition: Concerns about unintended consequences from AI use, including decreased human interaction, reduced analytical effort, and dependency risks that may undermine core learning objectives.
evidence: [Habib2025] 'ChatGPT's inherent strengths in efficiency and speed, while frequently compromising accuracy by being prone to errors'
[ElIdrissi2025] 'AI use shifted student behaviors toward information consumption rather than collaborative knowledge construction'

themes.name: Generative AI as Scaffolding Mechanism
themes.definition: Using AI tools to provide adaptive conceptual guidance, technical support, and reflective prompts that evolve with learner needs in skill acquisition processes.
evidence: [Khor2025] 'scaffolding strategies focused on enhancing conceptual understanding fostered engagement and programming skill development'
[Calderón-Oliver2025] 'helped students focus the search and improve the structure and quality of the works presented'
[Cohn2025] 'log-contextualized RAG improved retrieval... allowing agents to deliver personalized guidance supporting critical thinking'

data.meta_observations: Multiple methodological gaps appear in the dataset (missing objectives, methods, results per quality notes), but explicit mentions of critical thinking mechanisms persist across 22/28 included papers. Unexpectedly high emphasis on disciplinary-specific AI applications compared to generic skill development frameworks.
data.grounding_notes: All evidence strictly sourced from explicitly stated content. Three articles lacked sufficient actionable text for meaningful theme attribution. Frequency patterns indicate strong disciplinary integration trend, contrasting with some earlier literature focusing on generic AI literacy models.
